text:
cheng: thinking out loud — I hacked up a small prototype that replaces our per-page prefetch bitmap with a compact "tilemap" that groups contiguous GPU-backed ranges. Goal: reduce fragmentation when we migrate hot slices to GPU and avoid tiny pinned ranges. sketch below and tradeoffs.

maria: ooh, can you paste the sketch?

cheng: sure — basic idea: maintain a sorted vector of tiles {start, len, hot_score}. Tiles can merge if adjacent and same residency state. Prefetch picks tiles not pages. cheap membership test via binary search; updates are localized. Advantages: fewer metadata entries, better coalescing when evict/restore.

ajay: sounds promising. how do you handle partial hits (tile partially resident)?

cheng: two strategies — split-on-write or maintain subpage mask inside tile. prototype does split-on-write to keep runtime simple; we can later add a 64-bit mask to avoid splits for small partials.

samir: split-on-write could blow up the metadata churn for models with lots of small attention heads. do we have numbers?

cheng: quick numbers from the run: baseline page-prefetch map = 2.8M entries for a 40GB working set. tilemap (avg tile 4 pages) = 720k entries. update ops dropped ~3.5x. But split-op rate increased ~1.4x on synthetic tiny-random workloads.

maria: where does this interact with the KV cache and batching? could prefetching larger tiles increase KV cache miss amplification?

cheng: yes — bigger tiles mean we may pull in unused KV. but the tile score is weighted by recent access density; low-density tiles are deprioritized. Also we can cap prefetch bytes per request (config: tile_prefetch_bytes_limit).

ajay: implementation-wise — is the tilemap per-tenant, per-GPU, or global?

cheng: proposal: per-tenant logical tilemap (sharded by hotset hash) + per-GPU residency view. Sync only deltas to avoid global locks. infra-bot: deploy-ci: note — ensure tilemap diffs fit into our existing delta-sync shadow protocol (max 64KB per heartbeat).

samir: what about eviction fairness? if tiles are large, tenants could hoard slots by pinning one big tile.

cheng: we add a soft-cap: max_tiles_per_tenant_active + an eviction split heuristic that prefers breaking large low-hot-score tiles first. also tenant quotas remain enforced at slot level.

maria: API changes? devs reading residency telemetry will need different counters — tile_count, avg_tile_size, split_events.

ajay: please add a small compatibility shim that exposes per-page counts for the telemetry bridge for 3 months.

cheng: good call. proto patch includes shim. quick snippet from proto: ```
// tile struct
struct Tile { uint64_t start_page; uint32_t page_len; float hot_score; uint64_t submask64; // optional
};

// merge rule (pseudocode)
if (adjacent(a,b) && same_state(a,b) && combined_len <= MAX_TILE_PAGES) merge(a,b);
```

samir: race window concerns — merging requires compare-and-swap across shard list; we need an async defrag walker to avoid blocking hot allocation paths.

cheng: implemented a non-blocking background coalescer that acquires shard RCU and commits compacted vector. Hot path does optimistic path: try-merge fastpath with CAS, fallback to enqueue for background coalescer.

maria: any perf regressions on small-batch latency?

cheng: microbench: steady-state tail latency +5% on 99th for tiny inference patterns (due to extra binary-search), but throughput improved ~8% and overall memory overhead down 12%. tradeoff seems acceptable but we should gate behind a runtime flag.

ajay: propose we do a canary on dedicated hosts with one tenant, watch split_events and tail-latency for 48h. if split_events > threshold -> revert. also add metric: tile_split_per_min.

samir: also log the avg_tile_size per tenant so SRE can detect anomalous hoarding.

cheng: plan: open PR with proto + shim + runtime-flag; canary job config + grafana dashboard. I'll post link when ready.

maria: :thumbsup: let us know if you want help on the canary job or dashboard panels.

infra-bot: deploy-notice: created canary cluster pool "tilemap-canary" (3 hosts) — remember to include feature-flag header.

cheng: thanks — will do.
